Same, Same, New, New

STS-MS8-L4-13001400-MSVPA-AGS-GBL-02 • MS Visual and Performing Arts: Music Grade 8 • Unity, Variety, and Balance in a Final Composition
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
Tonight's round is called Build the Perfect Piece. Each composer is handed four instruments from four different parts of the world and three minutes to arrange them into one short piece. The judges award points for unity when an idea comes back, for variety when it changes, and for balance when no instrument buries the others.
If you could bring one instrument from anywhere in the world into your piece, which one would you choose, and where would you make it come back a second time?
Optional. You do not have to record this one.
1
What is Mei doing?
Look at the picture. Justify Mei's action and explain its purpose here. Use exact words for what her finger touches, not "thing" or "it".
2
What is Jelani holding?
Look at the picture. Justify what Jelani is holding and explain its role in the piece. Use the instrument's exact name.
3
What is the teacher doing?
Look at the picture. Justify the teacher's action and explain what it controls. Use exact words for the object and the reading she has set.
4
Where are these students? How do you know?
Look at the picture. Justify where these students are and cite two exact details as evidence.
5
Tell me about the Phrase Wall.
Look at the picture. Justify how the four lines differ and explain what a composer would call that difference. Use exact terms.
6
Tell me about what Linh is wearing.
Look at the picture. Justify what Linh is wearing and explain, with exact detail, how her clothing sets her apart from the others.
Record an answer for each question, then submit.
Content alignment: MU:Cr3.2.8 — Present the final version of a composition, song, or arrangement, demonstrating unity and variety, tension and release, and balance. ELD (Speaking — official ELPAC “Talk About a Scene”): PI.A.1, PII.B.3, PII.B.4, PII.B.5.
